tasks.prompt: Order the emergency disinfection response after a treatment plant contamination event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada responding to a suspected contamination of the clearwell during maintenance.
tasks.configuration: Scope: event discovery through the plant returned to normal service.

cards.label: Stop treated water leaving the plant and notify the operator in charge and the provincial contact as the emergency plan directs in general terms
Isolate the affected clearwell cell or storage from the rest of the system
Sample the affected water for chlorine residual and microbiological indicators before any correction
Raise disinfection in the isolated water to the emergency plan level and hold the directed contact time
Resample and confirm acceptable results, then flush or waste the affected water as directed
Return the plant to service in stages, document the event fully, and review the maintenance procedure that allowed it

tasks.explanation: Emergency response isolates first and samples before correcting, so evidence is preserved, disinfected water is proven by resampling, and return to service is staged and documented.

tasks.prompt: Order a filter performance evaluation for a dual media filter plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Alberta evaluating four dual media filters against each other.
tasks.configuration: Scope: evaluation planning through ranked filters and assigned actions.

cards.label: Set the evaluation measures: filtered turbidity, headloss growth, run length, backwash water use, and ripening time
Gather one month of run records for every filter and check the records are complete and comparable
Run each filter through one observed cycle with individual turbidity and headloss readings at set intervals
Compare filters on the same measures and identify the strongest and weakest performers
Inspect the weakest filter media and underdrain indicators before assigning a cause
Rank the filters, assign corrective actions with dates, and file the evaluation report

tasks.explanation: Filters are compared on identical measures over the same kind of cycle, and the weakest unit is inspected before any cause is assigned, so actions rest on evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter run optimization program balancing run length and quality.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan seeking longer filter runs without filtered quality loss.
tasks.configuration: Scope: baseline runs through the adopted run termination settings.

cards.label: Record baseline run length, terminal headloss, filtered turbidity profile, and wash water use for each filter
Confirm settled water quality is stable, since run length cannot be judged on a changing filter load
Extend the run termination limit by one small step on one filter only
Track filtered turbidity through the extended portion of the run at close intervals
Adopt the extension only if turbidity stays in band to the new limit, otherwise return to the prior limit
Apply the proven setting to the remaining filters and record the new termination rules in the filter program

tasks.explanation: Run optimization extends one filter by one step under stable settled quality, and the new limit is adopted plant wide only after turbidity proves the extension is safe.

tasks.prompt: Order the backwash optimization study for a gravity filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional gravity filter plant in Manitoba using more wash water than its program target.
tasks.configuration: Scope: baseline wash review through adopted wash settings.

cards.label: Measure current wash rate, duration, bed expansion, and total wash volume for a baseline wash
Observe waste water turbidity through the wash and note when it clears relative to the wash end
Check the cleaned bed by headloss at the start of the next run and by media surface inspection
Shorten or lower the wash by one step and repeat the waste turbidity and headloss checks
Confirm filtered quality and ripening time are unchanged at the reduced wash
Adopt the reduced settings, record wash volume savings, and set the next review date

tasks.explanation: Wash water is cut only after waste turbidity shows when cleaning is actually finished, and the reduced wash must still prove itself by clean bed headloss and unchanged filtered quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter media core sampling program for a plant wide survey.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada surveying media condition in all filters before a capital decision.
tasks.configuration: Scope: survey planning through the media condition report.

cards.label: Drain the first filter to just below the media surface using the planned shutdown sequence
Take core samples at a grid of points covering the centre, edges, and areas near the wash troughs
Measure media depth at each point and examine cores for mudballs, fouling, and layer mixing
Wash and sieve a core portion where the program requires a size check and record the result
Repeat the same grid and checks on every filter so results are comparable
Compile the condition report with depth maps and findings and recommend top up, cleaning, or replacement by filter

tasks.explanation: A comparable grid on every filter turns core sampling into a plant wide survey, and the report recommends work filter by filter from measured depths and core condition.

tasks.prompt: Order the particle counting program used to verify filter performance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia fitting particle counters to settled and filtered water lines.
tasks.configuration: Scope: instrument set up through particle trends in routine use.

cards.label: Install sample taps that deliver a steady, bubble free flow to the settled and filtered counters
Set counter size channels and flow rates to the instrument program and confirm sample flow is stable
Run the counters alongside grab turbidity samples and compare trends before trusting the counts
Set plant action levels for filtered counts based on the comparison period
Trend counts through filter runs to detect early breakthrough before turbidity responds
Review counter data monthly, clean and check the sensors, and file the performance summary

tasks.explanation: Particle counters earn trust by running against grab turbidity first; once action levels are set from that comparison, counts give an earlier breakthrough warning than turbidity alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the individual filter turbidity trending routine for a production day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada trending each filter separately rather than only the combined effluent.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start of day readings through end of day filter decisions.

cards.label: Record each filter starting turbidity, headloss, rate, and hours in service
Plot individual turbidity at the set interval and mark any filter trending above the plant band
Check a rising filter rate and settled quality to separate a load effect from a filter effect
Reduce rate or prepare to wash the first filter that approaches its turbidity or headloss limit
Wash filters in the order the trends dictate rather than by fixed rotation alone
Close the day with run lengths and wash reasons recorded for every filter

tasks.explanation: Individual trending catches one failing filter that combined effluent would hide, and wash order follows the trends, with rate and settled checks separating load effects from filter effects.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter to waste optimization for plants with limited waste capacity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan where filter to waste volume competes with a small residuals system.
tasks.configuration: Scope: ripening study through the adopted filter to waste rule.

cards.label: Measure filtered turbidity at short intervals from the start of a run to learn the true ripening profile
Identify the time and turbidity at which filtered water first meets the plant target consistently
Set the filter to waste end point at that proven turbidity with a safety margin, not at a fixed long time
Trial the rule on one filter and confirm clearwell turbidity is unaffected
Apply the rule to all filters and record waste volumes saved against the baseline
Re study the ripening profile after any media or pretreatment change and update the rule

tasks.explanation: The waste period is set from the measured ripening profile of the actual filters, proven on one unit, and restudied whenever media or pretreatment changes.

tasks.prompt: Order the dual media inspection and top up sequence during a filter outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional dual media filter in Alberta opened for anthracite loss found at a core survey.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filter drained through the topped up filter returned to service.

cards.label: Drain the filter and measure anthracite and sand depths at the survey grid points
Skim or remove fouled surface material and inspect the interface for mixing or mudballs
Add new anthracite in layers to restore the design depth and level the surface evenly
Fill the filter slowly from below to avoid disturbing the restored bed
Backwash gently at first, then at the normal rate, until waste water runs clear and fines are removed
Run filter to waste, confirm turbidity meets target, and return the filter to production with depths recorded

tasks.explanation: Top up restores measured depth layer by layer, and the bed is refilled gently and washed in stages so the new media is clean and settled before production resumes.

tasks.prompt: Order the membrane integrity monitoring program for a low pressure membrane plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ultrafiltration plant in western Canada running direct integrity tests on its membrane trains.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program set up through a failed train isolated and repaired.

cards.label: Set the direct integrity test method, test pressure, and pass limit for the membrane trains
Run baseline integrity tests on every train and record permeate turbidity trends alongside
Schedule routine tests at the program frequency and after any permeate turbidity excursion
Take any train that fails its test out of service and isolate it from the permeate header
Locate the failure by module testing, repair or replace the failed element, and retest the train
Return the train to service only on a passing test and file all results in the membrane program record

tasks.explanation: Integrity monitoring pairs routine direct tests with permeate trending, and a failed train stays isolated until a repair is proven by a passing retest.

tasks.prompt: Order the commissioning sequence for a rehabilitated filter returning to service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter in Manitoba returning after underdrain and media rehabilitation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: completed construction through the filter accepted for production.

cards.label: Inspect underdrains, nozzles, and support layers and confirm construction debris is fully removed
Place media in layers to design depths and level and record as built depths
Fill slowly from below, then disinfect and soak the cell as the commissioning plan directs
Wash the new bed repeatedly until waste water runs clear and fines are gone
Run filter to waste with turbidity sampling and confirm results meet target across a full test run
Accept the filter for production, file the commissioning record, and set its first performance review

tasks.explanation: Commissioning proves a rebuilt filter in stages: clean structure, correct media, disinfection, washing, and a full test run on filter to waste before the plant accepts it.

tasks.prompt: Order the receiving sequence for a bulk chemical delivery.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada receiving a bulk coagulant delivery by tanker.
tasks.configuration: Scope: truck arrival through the delivery recorded and storage returned to normal.

cards.label: Verify the delivery paperwork matches the order: product, strength, and quantity
Inspect the tanker fittings and confirm the receiving tank has room and the correct fill line is identified
Take a sample from the tanker and check appearance and strength against the product specification
Connect to the correct fill line, open containment, and stay present through the transfer
Confirm the receiving tank level rise matches the delivered quantity and close and secure the fill line
Record product, quantity, lot, and tank levels in the chemical log and file the delivery documents

tasks.explanation: Receiving proves identity and strength before transfer, watches the transfer with containment ready, and reconciles level rise against the paperwork before the delivery is closed.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical inventory and reorder program for a treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Saskatchewan managing coagulant, chlorine, and softening chemicals.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly inventory through a placed and confirmed reorder.

cards.label: Measure every bulk tank, day tank, and dry storage quantity on the weekly inventory day
Calculate days of supply for each chemical from current use rates and storage on hand
Compare days of supply with the reorder point that covers delivery lead time plus a safety margin
Prepare the order for any chemical at or below its reorder point and have it approved by the operator in charge
Confirm the order and delivery date with the supplier and note the expected arrival in the plant log
On delivery, receive the chemical under the receiving procedure and update the inventory record

tasks.explanation: Reorder points are built from measured stock, actual use rates, and delivery lead time, so ordering happens before urgency and every delivery closes the inventory loop.

tasks.prompt: Order the metering pump calibration program for liquid chemical feeds.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Alberta calibrating chlorine and coagulant metering pumps on a quarterly program.
tasks.configuration: Scope: calibration planning through all duty pumps verified.

cards.label: List every duty and standby feed pump and its chemical, set rate range, and calibration due date
Take one pump at a time and draw from its calibration column for a timed interval at the operating set point
Calculate delivered rate from drawdown and compare with the pump setting and the dose calculation
Adjust stroke or speed to correct any error and repeat the drawdown to confirm the correction
Repeat the check at a low and a high set point where the pump operates across a range
Record as found and as left rates, update due dates, and return the pump to normal service

tasks.explanation: Calibration measures delivered rate by timed drawdown, corrects and remeasures at the same set point, and records as found and as left values so dose records can be trusted.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation of a diluted chemical solution in a day tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing a polymer or hypochlorite day tank solution at a set strength.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty day tank through the solution in feed service.

cards.label: Calculate the chemical and water quantities for the target strength and tank volume and record the calculation
Fill the tank with the measured water quantity first where the procedure requires water first
Add the measured chemical slowly with mixing running and protective equipment in place
Mix for the full program time and allow any required ageing or settling period
Verify the solution strength by the program test or by a confirmed feed drawdown after start
Label the tank with product, strength, and preparation date and record the batch in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: Solution preparation is calculated before it is mixed, verified after ageing, and labelled with strength and date, so a feed problem can always be traced to a known batch.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical spill response sequence inside a treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba responding to a hypochlorite spill in the chemical room.
tasks.configuration: Scope: spill discovery through the area returned to service.

cards.label: Alert nearby staff, keep people clear, and put on the protective equipment listed for the product
Stop the source if it can be done safely, such as closing a valve or stopping the feed pump
Contain the spill with the room berm or spill kit so it cannot reach a drain or doorway
Notify the operator in charge and follow the product safety data sheet for cleanup and any reporting
Clean and neutralize the area as directed, collect cleanup material for proper disposal, and ventilate the room
Inspect the failed fitting or hose, record the event, and return the area to service only when it is clean and safe

tasks.explanation: Spill response protects people first, stops and contains the source, and cleans up under the safety data sheet, with the failed equipment inspected before the area reopens.

tasks.prompt: Order the qualification sequence before switching to a new chemical supplier product.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada qualifying an alternate coagulant product offered by a new supplier.
tasks.configuration: Scope: product documents received through the qualification decision.

cards.label: Review the product specification, safety data sheet, and drinking water suitability documentation for the offered product
Run jar tests comparing the new product with the current product on the same raw waters
Compare delivered cost per treated volume at the doses the jar tests require, not per container price
Trial the leading product at plant scale with feed calibration confirmed for its strength and density
Confirm settled and filtered quality, sludge character, and feed reliability through the trial period
Approve or reject the product in writing, update the chemical program if approved, and file the evidence

tasks.explanation: Qualification demands bench equivalence, true cost at the required dose, and a plant trial with calibrated feed before a product earns a place in the chemical program.

tasks.prompt: Order the preventive maintenance program round for chemical feed systems.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Saskatchewan running a monthly feed system maintenance round.
tasks.configuration: Scope: round planning through deficiencies corrected or scheduled.

cards.label: List every feed system due this month: pumps, day tanks, lines, valves, and containment
Inspect each pump for leaks, worn tubing or diaphragms, and steady operation, and check calibration due dates
Flush and inspect feed lines and injection points for scale, blockage, or backflow device faults
Check tank level gauges, vents, and secondary containment condition and drainage
Correct minor faults during the round and raise work orders for anything needing parts or shutdown
Record the round, close completed items, and carry open items to the next monthly list

tasks.explanation: The monthly round inspects delivery, injection, and containment together, fixes small faults on the spot, and carries the rest forward as tracked work orders.

tasks.prompt: Order a chemical dosage audit using plant mass balance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in Alberta auditing whether recorded coagulant dose matches chemical actually used.
tasks.configuration: Scope: audit period selection through audit findings actioned.

cards.label: Select an audit period and total the treated water volume for that period
Total chemical used from tank level change plus deliveries received in the same period
Calculate the average delivered dose from chemical mass used divided by treated volume
Compare the delivered dose with the average of the doses recorded in the daily logs
Investigate any gap by checking pump calibration, tank gauge accuracy, and log practices in that order
Correct the cause found, note the audit in the chemical program file, and set the next audit date

tasks.explanation: A mass balance audit compares what the tanks actually lost with what the logs claim, and investigates calibration and gauging before questioning the operators records.

tasks.prompt: Order the polymer make down and ageing sequence for a dry polymer system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada preparing dry polymer solution for flocculation aid service.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dry hopper check through aged solution feeding the process.

cards.label: Check dry polymer stock, hopper condition, and wetting water supply before starting the batch
Start wetting water and eductor flow, then start the dry feed at the program rate so powder wets without clumping
Fill the mix tank to level and mix for the full programme mixing time
Transfer the batch to the ageing tank and hold it for the full ageing period before use
Confirm solution appearance is uniform with no fisheyes or undissolved material
Place the aged solution in feed service, confirm delivery by drawdown, and record the batch

tasks.explanation: Dry polymer must wet without clumping, mix fully, and age before use; feeding unaged solution wastes product and weakens floc, so the sequence protects each stage in order.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter chemical storage management program for an unheated outbuilding.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in northern Manitoba storing liquid chemicals in a building that can fall below freezing.
tasks.configuration: Scope: autumn preparation through spring stand down.

cards.label: List every stored chemical and its freeze sensitivity and minimum storage temperature from its safety data sheet
Move freeze sensitive products to heated storage or provide inspected tank and line heating
Insulate and heat trace exposed feed lines and confirm the tracing works before the first cold period
Check building heat, alarms, and low temperature notification weekly through the winter
Inspect stored product after any cold event for freezing, crystallization, or container damage before use
Record the winter checks and stand the program down in spring with a condition report

tasks.explanation: Winter storage management starts from each product freeze limit, protects tanks and lines before the cold arrives, and verifies product condition after any cold event before the chemical is used.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily laboratory QA routine before bench testing begins.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant laboratory in western Canada starting its daily testing round.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entering the laboratory through the first samples accepted for analysis.

cards.label: Check reagent expiry dates, standard stocks, and glassware cleanliness for the day tests
Run the turbidimeter and pH meter start up checks with the program standards
Analyse a quality control standard for each test and confirm results fall inside control limits
Review sample log in times and holding times and prioritize samples closest to their limits
Begin sample analysis only for tests whose quality control passed
Record all start up checks and quality control results in the laboratory QA log

tasks.explanation: Daily QA proves instruments and reagents with control standards before any sample is run, and samples near holding time limits are prioritized once testing is cleared.

tasks.prompt: Order the turbidimeter calibration verification program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory in Saskatchewan verifying bench and online turbidimeters on a monthly program.
tasks.configuration: Scope: standards preparation through instruments returned to service.

cards.label: Prepare or verify the calibration standards and check their expiry and condition
Calibrate the bench turbidimeter with the standard series in order from lowest to highest
Verify the calibration with an independent check standard not used in the calibration
Compare the online turbidimeter with a bench grab sample taken at the same point and time
Adjust or service the online instrument if the comparison exceeds the program tolerance
Record calibration, verification, and comparison results with dates and analyst initials

tasks.explanation: Calibration is verified with an independent standard, and the online instrument is judged against a same point bench sample, so neither instrument is trusted on its own word.

tasks.prompt: Order the duplicate and spike quality control program for a monthly test batch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory in Alberta running monthly quality control on alkalinity and hardness testing.
tasks.configuration: Scope: batch planning through quality control acceptance or rerun.

cards.label: Select the samples for duplicate analysis and the sample to receive a known spike addition
Analyse the batch in the normal sequence with duplicates placed blind in the run
Analyse the spiked sample and calculate spike recovery from the measured increase
Calculate duplicate agreement and compare both duplicate agreement and recovery with program limits
Accept the batch if both measures pass; if either fails, investigate the method step and rerun the affected samples
File the quality control results with the batch record and trend them on the laboratory control charts

tasks.explanation: Duplicates prove precision and spikes prove accuracy on real samples; a batch is accepted only when both pass, and failures trigger a method investigation before results are released.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory control chart program for chlorine residual testing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory in western Canada charting a daily chlorine quality control standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: chart set up through an out of control response.

cards.label: Analyse the same quality control standard daily under the normal residual method
Plot each result on the control chart with the established mean and warning and control limits
Watch for results beyond control limits, or runs and trends that the program rules define as out of control
When a rule is triggered, stop reporting sample results from the method until the cause is checked
Check standards, reagents, and instrument condition, correct the cause, and rerun the control standard
Resume reporting only when the control standard is back in limits and record the event on the chart

tasks.explanation: A control chart turns daily standard results into an early warning system: defined rules stop reporting, the cause is corrected, and a passing standard restarts the method.

tasks.prompt: Order the alkalinity titration quality sequence for a new bench analyst.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new analyst in a Manitoba plant laboratory being checked on the alkalinity titration.
tasks.configuration: Scope: analyst preparation through results accepted into the plant record.

cards.label: Prepare the acid titrant and confirm its standardization record is current
Run a blank and a known alkalinity standard and confirm both meet the program expectations
Analyse the sample in duplicate with careful end point technique
Compare the duplicate results against the program agreement limit
Have a second analyst analyse a split of the same sample and compare results
Accept the analyst results into the plant record only when standard, duplicates, and split all pass

tasks.explanation: A new analyst earns acceptance in layers: current standardization, a passing standard, agreeing duplicates, and a matching split sample from a second analyst.

tasks.prompt: Order the sample preservation and holding time control program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional sampling program in western Canada sending samples to the plant lab and an external lab.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bottle preparation through results received within holding limits.

cards.label: Prepare labelled bottles with the correct preservative for each test and a chain of custody form
Collect samples at the program points, fill bottles as the method directs, and record time and conditions
Cool and store samples at the required temperature immediately after collection
Transport or analyse samples so every test starts inside its holding time, prioritizing the shortest limits
Check holding compliance when results arrive and qualify any result that missed its limit
File custody forms and results together and review missed limits at the monthly program review

tasks.explanation: Preservation, cooling, and holding times protect the sample from the moment of collection; results are only filed as valid when the custody record proves those limits were met.

tasks.prompt: Order the microbiological sampling quality program for a distribution system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional distribution sampling program in British Columbia under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly sampling round planning through results reviewed.

cards.label: Select the program sample sites for the week, rotating sites as the sampling plan directs
Use sterile bottles containing dechlorinating agent and check bottle expiry before leaving the plant
Flush the sample tap as the plan directs, collect without rinsing the bottle or touching its mouth, and record residual at the same tap
Transport samples cooled and within the program time limit to the laboratory
Review results on receipt and act on any positive result under the resampling and notification steps in the sampling plan
File results, residuals, and site records together and update the site rotation record

tasks.explanation: Microbiological quality depends on sterile technique, dechlorinated bottles, and paired residual readings, and any positive result follows the plan resampling steps without delay.

tasks.prompt: Order the instrument calibration log program for plant laboratory and online instruments.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Saskatchewan consolidating calibration records for bench and online instruments.
tasks.configuration: Scope: instrument inventory through the monthly overdue review.

cards.label: List every bench and online instrument with its calibration method, interval, and responsible person
Enter each completed calibration in the log with date, standards used, as found and as left results
Flag instruments approaching their due date at the weekly operations meeting
Remove from service, or qualify results from, any instrument that passes its due date uncalibrated
Calibrate overdue instruments and review whether results since the due date need qualification
Review the log monthly with the operator in charge and file the signed review

tasks.explanation: A single calibration log with due date flags and overdue consequences keeps every reported result traceable to an instrument that was in calibration when the result was produced.

tasks.prompt: Order the split sample proficiency program with an external laboratory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant laboratory in Alberta comparing its results with an external laboratory twice a year.
tasks.configuration: Scope: split round planning through corrective actions closed.

cards.label: Collect a well mixed sample large enough for both laboratories and split it into matched portions
Preserve, label, and ship the external portion under chain of custody while analysing the plant portion the same day
Record plant results without seeing the external results first
Compare results test by test against the program agreement limits when the external report arrives
Investigate any test outside limits by reviewing method, calibration, and quality control records for that date
Complete corrective actions, document the round, and file it in the laboratory QA record

tasks.explanation: Split samples test the whole plant method against an outside laboratory; plant results are recorded blind, and disagreements are investigated from the records of the actual analysis date.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory data review and reporting sequence for treated water results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory in western Canada releasing a week of treated water results.
tasks.configuration: Scope: raw bench results through results reported and filed.

cards.label: Check bench sheets for completeness: sample identity, times, analyst, and method for every result
Verify calculations and unit conversions on a sample of results against the bench data
Confirm quality control for each test day passed and flag any result tied to a failed control
Compare treated results with plant targets and guideline values in general terms and highlight excursions
Report the reviewed results to the operator in charge with excursions and qualifiers clearly marked
File the signed results with bench sheets and quality control records as one traceable package

tasks.explanation: Data review checks identity, calculations, and quality control before results are compared with targets, so the operator in charge receives results that are already proven traceable.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for high settled water turbidity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional conventional plant in western Canada where settled turbidity rose while filtered quality is still holding.
tasks.configuration: Scope: confirmed settled rise through settled quality restored.

cards.label: Confirm settled turbidity with a fresh sample and check raw turbidity, pH, and alkalinity for a source change
Run a jar test on current raw water to test whether the plant dose still fits the water
Verify coagulant and aid feed delivery by drawdown against the recorded doses
Inspect floc size and character and clarifier blanket depth and surface condition
Correct the first proven cause: dose, feed delivery, or blanket control, in that evidence order
Recheck settled turbidity after a detention time and trend it until it returns to band, then log the diagnosis

tasks.explanation: The program tests water, dose, delivery, and blanket in order and corrects the first proven cause, rather than changing dose and withdrawal at the same time.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for a filter showing early breakthrough.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional gravity filter in Saskatchewan breaking through at half its normal run length.
tasks.configuration: Scope: breakthrough confirmed through the filter returned to normal runs.

cards.label: Confirm breakthrough on the individual filter turbidity record and a grab sample
Check settled turbidity and filtration rate to learn whether the filter is overloaded or underloaded
Review the last backwash record and observe a wash for rate, expansion, and waste clearing
Inspect the drained bed surface for mudballs, cracking, or media loss if the wash looks normal
Check pretreatment floc condition, since weak pin floc passes a sound filter
Correct the proven cause, run a monitored test run, and record the diagnosis and run result

tasks.explanation: Early breakthrough is traced through load, wash, bed, and floc in that order, because each cause produces the same symptom but needs a different fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the taste and odour event troubleshooting program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba responding to earthy taste complaints during an algae increase in the reservoir.
tasks.configuration: Scope: complaints received through taste and odour controlled and monitoring set.

cards.label: Log complaint locations and character and sample raw and treated water for odour at the plant
Check reservoir conditions and recent raw results for algae or turnover changes that explain the event
Confirm powdered activated carbon or oxidant systems, where fitted, are available and feeding correctly
Run bench tests to set the carbon dose or treatment adjustment for the current raw odour
Apply the adjustment and monitor treated odour and customer reports daily
Hold the treatment until raw odour returns to normal, then step it down and record the event playbook

tasks.explanation: Taste and odour work starts by matching complaint character to raw water evidence, sets treatment by bench test, and steps treatment down only when the source event has passed.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for low chlorine residual in distribution.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional system in western Canada where far end residuals fell while the plant outlet residual stayed on target.
tasks.configuration: Scope: low residuals confirmed through system residuals restored.

cards.label: Confirm far end results with fresh samples and record water temperature and sample point conditions
Map low results by area and compare with storage levels and water age in those areas
Check plant outlet residual, dose records, and feed calibration to prove the plant is delivering its target
Inspect the serving reservoir turnover and mixing and sample its inlet and outlet residuals
Flush low residual areas in a planned sequence and resample after flushing
Correct the proven cause, such as turnover or dose, trend the area for a week, and log the diagnosis

tasks.explanation: When the plant outlet is on target, the search moves outward through water age, storage turnover, and local flushing, correcting the storage or age cause the evidence proves.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for a chemical feed that is under delivering.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional coagulant feed in Alberta where settled quality drifted and the day tank level fell more slowly than expected.
tasks.configuration: Scope: suspected under delivery through delivery proven restored.

cards.label: Compare day tank level change with treated volume to estimate the delivered dose
Run a calibration drawdown at the operating set point and compare delivered rate with the setting
Inspect suction lines, foot valves, and strainers for blockage or air leaks if delivery is low
Check pump tubing, diaphragm, or drive condition and the injection point for scale or blockage
Repair or replace the faulty part and repeat the drawdown until delivery matches the setting
Recheck settled quality after a detention time and record the fault and repair in the feed log

tasks.explanation: Under delivery is proven by tank accounting and drawdown before parts are changed, and the repair is only closed when drawdown and settled quality both confirm it.

tasks.prompt: Order the algae bloom response program for a prairie reservoir plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan facing a summer algae bloom with rising filter clogging and taste risk.
tasks.configuration: Scope: bloom indicators confirmed through bloom season operating settings set.

cards.label: Confirm bloom indicators: raw algae counts or appearance, pH swings, taste and odour, and shortening filter runs
Adjust intake depth or source blend where the plant has options to draw cleaner water
Run jar tests to reset coagulant and aid doses for algae laden water and check alkalinity support
Shorten filter run limits and increase backwash readiness for the higher solids and algae load
Add or adjust taste and odour treatment where fitted and increase treated odour checks
Review bloom indicators weekly and hold the settings until indicators return to normal, then step back and log the season response

tasks.explanation: Bloom response combines source selection, reset coagulation, shorter filter runs, and odour control, and holds all of them until source indicators, not the calendar, say the bloom has passed.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for a treated water pH excursion.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada where finished pH moved outside its band over one shift.
tasks.configuration: Scope: excursion confirmed through pH stable in band and cause recorded.

cards.label: Confirm finished pH with a freshly calibrated bench meter and a second sample
Check raw pH and alkalinity and the coagulant dose, since coagulation consumes alkalinity
Verify alkalinity supplement or lime feed delivery by drawdown or timed output
Check softening or recarbonation performance where those processes set the final pH
Correct the proven feed or dose cause in a small step and recheck pH after the process detention time
Increase pH sampling until three consecutive results are in band and record the diagnosis

tasks.explanation: A pH excursion is traced through raw alkalinity, coagulant demand, and each pH setting feed in order, with small corrections judged only after detention time has passed.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for recurring coloured water after filter runs start.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia where a brief colour spike follows each filter return to service.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pattern confirmed through colour controlled at run starts.

cards.label: Confirm the pattern by sampling filtered colour at short intervals from a run start
Check whether the filter was run to waste and for how long, and review the ripening record
Inspect the bed for iron or manganese deposits and check backwash effectiveness for the cell
Check oxidant residual at the filter influent, since low residual lets metals pass early in the run
Extend filter to waste or correct the wash or oxidant cause the evidence supports
Verify colour at run start on the next two runs and record the fix in the filter log

tasks.explanation: A start of run colour spike points to ripening, deposits, or oxidant at the bed; each is checked in order and the fix is proven across the next two run starts.

tasks.prompt: Order the clarifier sludge blanket upset troubleshooting program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional clarifier in Manitoba whose blanket rose and began washing over the weirs.
tasks.configuration: Scope: upset confirmed through blanket control restored.

cards.label: Measure blanket depth across the basin and settled turbidity at the effluent
Check raw flow and recent flow changes, since a hydraulic surge lifts an established blanket
Check sludge withdrawal rate, pump operation, and sludge line for blockage
Check solids loading from coagulation dose and raw turbidity changes
Increase withdrawal in steps if withdrawal is the proven limit, or reduce flow if hydraulics are the cause
Remonitor blanket and settled quality until both are in band and record the cause and settings

tasks.explanation: Blanket upset has hydraulic, withdrawal, and loading causes; the program measures all three and corrects only the one the evidence proves, in steps with remonitoring.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting program for shortened filter runs across the whole plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Alberta where every filter run shortened over the same week.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant wide pattern confirmed through normal run lengths restored.

cards.label: Confirm the pattern from run records and rule out a single filter fault by comparing all filters
Check settled water turbidity and particle load, since a plant wide cause usually sits upstream of the filters
Review coagulant dose, jar test currency, and raw water changes for the same period
Check backwash water supply and confirm washes are reaching full rate on every filter
Correct the proven upstream or wash cause and monitor the next full cycle on two filters
Record the diagnosis and restore normal run termination settings once runs recover

tasks.explanation: When all filters shorten together, the cause is shared: settled load, coagulation, or wash supply, and the program proves it on two monitored cycles before closing.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator in charge daily supervisory routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge at a Class 2 plant in western Canada starting the production day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving on shift through the day plan issued to the team.

cards.label: Review overnight logs, alarms, treated volumes, and any outstanding samples or maintenance
Check clearwell and storage levels, chemical inventories, and the day demand forecast
Walk the plant with the shift operator and confirm process status at each unit
Set the day priorities: production targets, sampling, maintenance support, and any process trials
Assign tasks with owners and check back times and note them on the day board
Close the routine by updating the operations log and flagging risks to the utility manager

tasks.explanation: The operator in charge builds the day from records, storage, and chemical facts first, then assigns owned tasks with check back times, so supervision starts from evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the shift coverage program when an operator absence is reported.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Saskatchewan covering a week of shifts after a sickness absence is reported.
tasks.configuration: Scope: absence reported through the covered roster confirmed to all staff.

cards.label: Confirm the shifts affected and the minimum certified coverage each shift requires in general terms
Check the roster for qualified operators available within working time limits
Offer the open shifts in the program order and record acceptances
Confirm no operator is scheduled beyond fatigue or hours limits by the coverage plan
Publish the revised roster to all affected staff and the operator in charge board
Log the absence coverage and review whether a standby list update is needed

tasks.explanation: Coverage protects certified minimums and fatigue limits first, fills shifts in the program order, and is only complete when every affected person has the revised roster.

tasks.prompt: Order the staff training and competency sign off program for a process task.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in Manitoba signing off a junior operator on filter backwashing.
tasks.configuration: Scope: training need identified through the competency record filed.

cards.label: Confirm the trainee has completed the procedure reading and safety requirements for the task
Demonstrate the full task at normal pace, explaining each check and decision point
Observe the trainee performing the task under direct supervision and correct technique on the spot
Have the trainee perform the task a second time with the supervisor observing without prompting
Question the trainee on abnormal situations, such as a wash that does not clear, and confirm sound responses
Sign the competency record, file it in the training file, and set any refresher date

tasks.explanation: Competency is signed only after an unprompted performance and abnormal situation questioning, so the record means the operator can handle the task and its failures.

tasks.prompt: Order the standard operating procedure review program for treatment processes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada reviewing its treatment standard operating procedures on an annual cycle.
tasks.configuration: Scope: review schedule set through revised procedures issued.

cards.label: List every treatment procedure with its last review date and owner
Have operators mark steps that no longer match the equipment or practice as actually performed
Compare marked procedures with current equipment, chemical products, and safety requirements
Draft revisions with operator input and check the revised steps in the field before approval
Approve, date, and issue the revised procedures and remove superseded copies from use points
Brief all shifts on changed procedures and file the review record

tasks.explanation: Procedure review starts from how the work is actually done, checks revisions in the field, and removes old copies, so the issued procedure and the plant practice become the same thing.

tasks.prompt: Order the regulatory sampling calendar management program for a treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Alberta managing its sampling calendar under provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual calendar build through monthly completion checks.

cards.label: List every required sample by parameter, location, and frequency from the plant sampling plan
Build the annual calendar spreading samples so no week carries an unmanageable load
Assign each sampling round an owner and a backup and enter reminders ahead of due dates
Check completion weekly and reschedule any missed sample inside its allowed window with a note
Review results as they return and file them against the calendar entries they satisfy
Close the year with a completion report and carry lessons into the next calendar build

tasks.explanation: Calendar management assigns owners and backups, checks completion weekly while missed samples can still be recovered, and files results against the entries they satisfy.

tasks.prompt: Order the incident reporting and notification sequence for an adverse water quality result.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in British Columbia receiving an adverse treated water result during the working day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: result received through the incident file closed.

cards.label: Verify the result by checking sample identity, quality control, and whether a confirmation sample is required
Notify the operator in charge immediately and begin the notification steps in the plant incident plan in general terms
Collect confirmation and follow up samples at the directed locations and times
Apply any directed corrective action, such as added disinfection or flushing, and record actions with times
Keep a single incident log of results, notifications, and actions in time order
Close the incident when follow up results and the responsible authority direction allow, and file the complete record

tasks.explanation: Incident handling verifies the result without delaying notification, keeps one time ordered log, and closes only on follow up results and direction, not on the corrective action alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the preventive maintenance planning program for a quarterly cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in western Canada planning quarterly preventive maintenance with the maintenance team.
tasks.configuration: Scope: asset list review through the quarter plan scheduled.

cards.label: List assets due for service this quarter from the maintenance register and their criticality
Group tasks that share a shutdown or a process outage so units are opened once
Check spare parts and consumables for the grouped tasks and order anything missing
Schedule the work with production, protecting storage and treatment capacity on work days
Issue work orders with owners, dates, and lockout requirements noted
Review completed work at quarter end and carry unfinished items forward with reasons

tasks.explanation: Quarterly planning groups work by shared outages, proves parts are on hand, and schedules around production, so maintenance does not create its own treatment risk.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly plant performance review led by the operator in charge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 2 plant in Saskatchewan reviewing treated volumes, quality, chemical use, and energy for the month.
tasks.configuration: Scope: data assembly through actions assigned for the next month.

cards.label: Assemble monthly treated volume, quality results, chemical use per volume, and filter and energy records
Compare each measure with the plant targets and with the same month in the prior year
Identify the two largest variances and check the operating records that explain them
Separate variances caused by raw water or demand events from those within operator control
Assign improvement actions with owners and dates for the controllable variances
Present the review to the team, file it, and carry open actions to the next monthly agenda

tasks.explanation: The monthly review explains variances from records before assigning actions, and only controllable causes get improvement actions, so effort lands where the team can change the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the emergency preparedness drill program for a plant power failure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba running a planned drill of its power failure response.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drill planning through the drill debrief actions assigned.

cards.label: Set the drill scenario, safety limits, and the rule that real emergencies override the drill at any time
Brief participants on the scenario start signal without revealing the drill injects
Start the drill and observe generator start, load transfer, and process protection steps
Record response times, communication steps, and any equipment that fails to perform
End the drill, restore normal line up, and confirm the plant is fully back in normal service
Debrief with participants, assign corrective actions with dates, and file the drill report

tasks.explanation: A drill is run like the real event but inside safety limits, is judged on observed times and equipment performance, and ends with the plant proven back in normal service.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical budget and ordering cycle review at quarter end.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in Alberta reviewing chemical spending and stock at quarter end.
tasks.configuration: Scope: usage records gathered through next quarter orders planned.

cards.label: Total each chemical used in the quarter from inventory records and deliveries
Calculate use per treated volume for each chemical and compare with the dose records
Compare spending with the quarter budget and explain variances from dose, volume, or price changes
Check stock on hand and open orders against the next quarter demand forecast
Plan next quarter orders and delivery timing around storage capacity and seasonal demand
File the review and brief the utility manager on variances and the order plan

tasks.explanation: The quarter review ties spending back to dose and volume, so a variance is explained as chemistry, demand, or price before the next quarter orders are planned.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter start up sequence for a plant in extreme cold.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in northern Saskatchewan starting production on a morning well below freezing after an overnight shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the plant through steady winter production.

cards.label: Check building heat, ventilation, and for any frozen or burst lines before starting equipment
Confirm chemical feed lines and day tanks are warm and product is flowing, not crystallized or frozen
Inspect the intake and raw line for ice restriction and confirm raw flow can be established
Start chemical feeds and confirm delivery by drawdown, allowing extra time for cold viscous product
Start raw flow at a reduced rate and watch pressures for ice related restriction
Raise to winter production rate once flows, doses, and treated quality are confirmed and log cold conditions

tasks.explanation: Cold start up proves heat, chemical flow, and intake freedom from ice before production, because a frozen line discovered under full flow becomes damage instead of a delay.

tasks.prompt: Order the intake frazil ice management program during a cold snap.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional river intake plant in western Canada managing frazil ice that can block intake screens.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cold snap forecast received through the event stood down.

cards.label: Monitor river temperature, air temperature, and intake differential level for frazil conditions
Reduce intake rate or cycle pumps where the program directs to limit ice adhesion
Apply the site ice control measures, such as screen raking, air bubbling, or warm water recirculation, in program order
Watch intake level and raw flow closely and switch to any standby intake or storage supply if blockage grows
Record ice conditions, measures used, and intake performance through the event
Stand the program down when temperatures moderate and inspect screens for ice damage

tasks.explanation: Frazil management watches the temperature and level signals that precede blockage, applies controls in program order, and protects supply with standby options before the intake is lost.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical feed freeze protection program for winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Manitoba protecting outdoor and unheated chemical feed lines through winter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: autumn preparation through a mid winter cold event check.

cards.label: List every feed line, pump, and tank exposed to freezing temperatures
Insulate lines and confirm heat tracing operates on each exposed run
Drain or protect any line that will sit idle with chemical in it during cold periods
Set a weekly winter check of tracing, insulation condition, and building heat alarms
After any extreme cold night, confirm each feed delivers by drawdown before relying on its dose
Record checks and any freeze damage and repair protection before the next cold period

tasks.explanation: Freeze protection inventories every exposed run before winter, proves heat tracing works, and rechecks delivery after cold nights, since a partly frozen line under delivers silently.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter building heat and ventilation winter program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional filter gallery in western Canada where condensation and freezing threaten instruments and valves.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seasonal set up through winter weekly checks.

cards.label: Check gallery heating units, louvers, and door seals before the heating season
Set ventilation to control humidity without dropping gallery temperature toward freezing
Identify cold spots at exterior walls, sample lines, and instrument taps and add protection where needed
Drain or heat trace small sample and drain lines that can freeze and burst
Walk the gallery weekly in winter checking temperature, condensation, and ice at doors and vents
Record winter checks and correct heating or ventilation faults as priority work orders

tasks.explanation: Gallery winter care balances heat against humidity, protects the small lines that freeze first, and turns weekly temperature walks into early warning for instruments and valves.

tasks.prompt: Order the cold water coagulation adjustment program for winter raw water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Alberta whose raw water falls near freezing with low turbidity and slow floc formation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winter jar testing through winter dose settings adopted.

cards.label: Run jar tests at actual winter raw temperature, since warm bench water hides cold water behaviour
Allow longer flocculation and settling times in the bench program to match cold reaction rates
Compare coagulant and aid combinations for floc that forms and settles at the cold condition
Set winter plant doses and consider aid addition from the cold bench results
Adjust plant flocculation to the gentler, longer pattern the cold tests support where equipment allows
Monitor settled quality closely for the first week and record the winter settings for the seasonal file

tasks.explanation: Cold water coagulation must be tested cold: reaction and settling slow down, so doses, aid, and flocculation settings come from bench work at the real winter temperature.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter access and delivery management program for a remote plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional remote plant in northern British Columbia that depends on a single access road for staff and chemical deliveries.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winter plan set through a storm delivery completed.

cards.label: Set the winter minimum chemical and fuel stocks that cover the longest expected road closure
Schedule autumn deliveries to reach winter stock levels before the first major storm period
Agree storm communication and road condition checks with staff and suppliers
During a storm closure, ration non essential chemical use and confirm essential treatment stocks daily
Receive the first post storm delivery under the full receiving procedure and rebuild stocks to winter levels
Review the winter stock performance in spring and reset minimum levels from the record

tasks.explanation: Remote winter planning stocks for the longest closure, not the average one, and treats the first post storm delivery as a stock rebuild, not just a routine receipt.

tasks.prompt: Order the standby power winter storm operating program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in Saskatchewan preparing for a forecast winter storm with outage risk.
tasks.configuration: Scope: storm forecast through the plant back on utility power.

cards.label: Test the standby generator under load and confirm fuel for the forecast outage duration
Fill treated storage toward the top of its operating range before the storm arrives
Confirm chemical stocks, heating fuel, and staff coverage for an extended event
On outage, confirm generator load transfer and shed non essential loads as the plan directs
Run the plant at the storm production rate that storage and generator capacity can sustain
On power return, transfer loads in stages, check all processes, and log the event and fuel used

tasks.explanation: Storm readiness is built before the outage: tested generation, full storage, and confirmed stocks, so the outage itself is run at a sustainable rate and closed with a staged return.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter distribution residual management program for cold, slow moving water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional system in western Canada where winter demand falls and water age rises in storage and dead ends.
tasks.configuration: Scope: autumn residual review through spring stand down.

cards.label: Map winter low demand areas, storage turnover times, and historic low residual points
Set winter reservoir operating levels and turnover cycles that limit water age
Schedule dead end and low use area flushing through the winter on a rotating list
Sample residuals at the mapped points more often through the cold period
Adjust plant outlet residual within its target band where sampling shows age driven loss
Review winter residual results in spring and update the low point map from the evidence

tasks.explanation: Winter residual loss is an age problem, so the program manages turnover and flushing at mapped low points and uses sampling, not complaints, to judge whether it worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the spring melt preparation program for a snowmelt driven source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada preparing in late winter for snowmelt turbidity and flow changes.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation checklist through the plant ready for melt conditions.

cards.label: Review last year melt records for turbidity peaks, dose ranges, and filter performance
Build chemical stocks, especially coagulant and alkalinity supplement, to melt season levels
Service jar test equipment and prepare dose ladder sheets for rapid melt jar testing
Inspect clarifier sludge handling and residuals capacity for the higher solids load
Confirm standby filters are ready and backwash supply can support shorter runs
Brief all shifts on melt triggers for dose changes and flow reduction and post the melt plan

tasks.explanation: Melt preparation stocks chemicals, readies residuals capacity for higher solids, and posts clear dose and flow triggers before the melt, so the event is managed, not improvised.

tasks.prompt: Settled turbidity at a Saskatchewan plant rose from 1.8 NTU to 4.6 NTU in two days while the alum dose stayed at the setting used all spring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: Raw turbidity rose from 24 NTU to 66 NTU as snowmelt runoff reached the river intake.
The alum feed setting was not changed during the two days.
A jar test series today settles to 1.4 NTU at a dose about 45 percent above the plant dose, and worse at the plant dose.
Floc in the basin is small and sparse and much of it stays suspended in a grab sample after 30 minutes.
Raw pH, alkalinity, rapid mix and flocculator operation are all in their usual ranges.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is excessive and particles have restabilized
The alum dose is now too low for the higher raw solids load
The flocculators are shearing floc that formed correctly
The settled turbidimeter has drifted high

inference.explanation: Raw turbidity nearly tripled on a fixed dose, floc is small and unsettled, and jars settle well only at a higher dose. Restabilization needs an excessive dose, shear would break floc that had formed, and a drifted meter would not match the unsettled grab sample.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms that the dose failed to track raw demand?

options.label: Archived filter backwash volume log
Archived jar test series and dose log from the last runoff event
Archived finished water hardness log

nextClue.explanation: Archived jar test series and dose log from the last runoff event directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Backwash volumes were normal, which says nothing about coagulant demand in the basin.
clueText.nc-b: Last runoff, the jar optimum rose with raw turbidity in the same way and raising the plant dose restored settled turbidity below 2 NTU.
clueText.nc-c: Hardness was steady and is unrelated to floc formation or settling.

tasks.prompt: Two days after the alum dose was doubled for turbid runoff at a Manitoba plant, floc collapsed and settled turbidity rose sharply.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: The alum dose was doubled two days ago and has stayed at the higher rate.
Raw alkalinity fell from 88 mg/L to 26 mg/L as CaCO3 and coagulation pH fell from 7.2 to 5.9.
The soda ash day bin is empty and its feeder shows a no-flow alarm that was acknowledged but not cleared.
Jar tests with added alkalinity form large, fast settling floc at the current alum dose, while jars without added alkalinity fail.
Raw turbidity is unchanged since the dose increase.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The higher alum dose restabilized particles by charge reversal
Cold raw water slowed the flocculation reaction
Alum consumed the alkalinity and, with no alkalinity replacement, pH dropped out of the effective coagulation range
The flocculator paddles are turning too fast and shearing floc

inference.explanation: Alkalinity fell by about two thirds and pH dropped after the dose doubled, the soda ash feeder is empty, and jars recover when alkalinity is added rather than when dose is cut. That rules against restabilization, and no temperature or paddle change is observed.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the alkalinity feed failure?

options.label: Archived raw water temperature log
Archived clarifier sludge blanket survey
Archived soda ash feeder run log and bin level record for the past week

nextClue.explanation: Archived soda ash feeder run log and bin level record for the past week directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Raw temperature held near 10 C all week, which does not explain an alkalinity loss of this size.
clueText.nc-b: The blanket survey was normal, which rules out a settling problem but does not track chemical feed.
clueText.nc-c: The feeder log shows no soda ash delivered for three days while alum feed doubled, and the bin record shows it empty from the first day.

tasks.prompt: In mid January at a northern Alberta plant, floc is weak and slow to form and settled turbidity is 4.1 NTU, although the same dose produced 1.3 NTU in October.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: Raw water temperature is 1 C, down from 15 C in October.
Jar tests at the current dose eventually form good floc but take about three times longer than in October.
Alum dose, rapid mix and flocculator settings match the October settings.
Raw turbidity, pH and alkalinity are similar to October values.
Extending flocculation time in the jar test restores settled turbidity to about 1.5 NTU.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum stock has lost strength over the winter
Raw alkalinity has been consumed by the alum dose
The sedimentation basin is short-circuiting
Cold water is slowing floc formation, so the available flocculation time is no longer enough

inference.explanation: Only temperature changed materially, jar floc forms well but slowly, and longer flocculation time restores performance. Alkalinity is unchanged, the same chemical works given time, and a short circuit would not slow floc growth in a jar.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms a seasonal cold water pattern?

options.label: Archived winter operating records of settled turbidity against raw temperature for three past winters
Archived alum delivery certificates
Archived distribution pressure log

nextClue.explanation: Archived winter operating records of settled turbidity against raw temperature for three past winters directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Each past winter, settled turbidity rose as raw water fell below 4 C and recovered in spring at the same dose, matching this year.
clueText.nc-b: Alum certificates show the product met specification, which does not explain a pattern tied to temperature.
clueText.nc-c: Distribution pressures were normal and have no bearing on floc formation time in the plant.

tasks.prompt: Settled turbidity worsened after an operator raised the alum dose twice to chase colour at a British Columbia interior plant, and the water now carries fine dispersed solids.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: The alum dose is now about double the jar test dose that worked last week.
A jar test series today shows settled turbidity lowest at a mid range dose and higher at both lower and higher doses.
Coagulation pH has fallen from 7.0 to 6.1 as the dose increased.
Floc at the current dose is tiny and dispersed and a settled sample stays cloudy for hours.
Raw colour and turbidity have been steady for two days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is excessive, restabilizing particles and depressing pH
The alum dose is still too low for the raw load
The flocculator is shearing large floc into fine floc
The clarifier sludge blanket has risen into the effluent launders

inference.explanation: The jar curve is U shaped with its best point well below the current dose, pH fell as dose rose, and solids stay dispersed. A low dose contradicts the lower jar optimum, shear needs large floc forming first, and no blanket observation is offered.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the overdose pattern?

options.label: Archived sludge blanket depth survey
Archived jar test dose curve and plant dose trend for the past week
Archived flocculator motor current log

nextClue.explanation: Archived jar test dose curve and plant dose trend for the past week directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Blanket depth was mid range and steady, which does not explain solids that will not settle in a jar.
clueText.nc-b: The archived curve shows settled turbidity rising steadily once the plant dose passed the jar optimum, exactly as this week.
clueText.nc-c: Flocculator current was normal, which argues against a mechanical mixing change.

tasks.prompt: Settled and filtered turbidity are acceptable at a prairie plant, but chlorine demand has jumped, coagulant demand is rising, and the raw water looks tea coloured.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: A 0.45 micron filtered raw sample still measures 30 CU of colour, close to the unfiltered value of 34 CU.
Raw turbidity is low at 3 NTU and has not changed.
Jar tests need a higher alum dose than usual, and the extra dose mainly removes colour rather than turbidity.
The reservoir is low after a dry summer and the intake is drawing from a deeper, more organic rich layer.
Raw dissolved organic carbon measures 6.9 mg/L, up from a usual 3.4 mg/L.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Suspended solids from runoff are overloading coagulation
Dissolved organic matter in the source has increased, raising both coagulant and chlorine demand
The alum stock solution has been diluted
The colour meter reads high because of turbidity interference

inference.explanation: Colour survives fine filtration, turbidity is low, dissolved organic carbon nearly doubled, and jars spend extra dose removing colour. Diluted alum would not raise chlorine demand, and turbidity interference is contradicted by the low turbidity and the filtered reading.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the source organic shift?

options.label: Archived raw dissolved organic carbon and colour log by intake depth
Archived alum tank refill records
Archived turbidity meter calibration record

nextClue.explanation: Archived raw dissolved organic carbon and colour log by intake depth directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the deep intake layer has run near 7 mg/L dissolved organic carbon all month, roughly double the shallow layer used in spring.
clueText.nc-b: Refill records show alum delivered at normal strength, which clears the chemical stock.
clueText.nc-c: The turbidity meter calibrated within tolerance, and turbidity is low in any case.

tasks.prompt: Floc quality fell steadily over two days at a plant using a cationic polymer aid, even though the alum dose sits exactly at the jar test optimum.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: Jar tests at the plant alum dose settle to 1.3 NTU when the polymer dose is halved, and to 4.2 NTU at the current polymer dose.
Floc at the plant polymer dose is stringy and gelatinous and floats in the jar instead of settling.
The polymer feed pump was replaced two days ago and its calibration was never checked after the change.
A drawdown test shows the new polymer pump delivers about twice the volume its setting indicates.
Raw turbidity, pH and alkalinity are steady.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is too low for the raw water
The polymer aid is overdosed and is restabilizing and floating the floc
The rapid mixer has failed
The raw water temperature has fallen sharply

inference.explanation: Halving the polymer in jars restores settling at the same alum dose, floc is stringy and floating, and the uncalibrated replacement pump delivers double its setting. Alum, mixing and temperature are not implicated by any observation.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the polymer delivery error?

options.label: Archived polymer pump maintenance and calibration records
Archived raw water temperature log
Archived alum delivery certificates

nextClue.explanation: Archived polymer pump maintenance and calibration records directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Records show the pump was swapped two days ago with no post repair calibration, and the same model ran high after a past swap until calibrated.
clueText.nc-b: Raw temperature was steady near 9 C through the decline.
clueText.nc-c: Alum certificates and jar results at the plant alum dose clear the alum feed.

tasks.prompt: Floc formation stopped almost completely over one shift at an Alberta plant even though the alum pump is running and stroking normally.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 2 water plant case: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review, and provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality apply in general terms.

evidence.label: The alum day tank level has not dropped at all during the shift.
Pressure at the pump discharge gauge is well above its normal reading.
No flow is visible at the injection point sample tap and the feed line past the pump is cool and still.
A jar test dosed by hand from the day tank forms normal floc at the usual dose.
Raw turbidity, pH and alkalinity are unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum in the day tank has lost its strength
The alum feed line or injection quill is plugged, so no coagulant reaches the water
The alum pump has lost its prime and is pumping air
Raw water demand rose beyond what the dose can treat

inference.explanation: The tank level is static, discharge pressure is high, and nothing arrives at the injection tap, while hand dosed tank chemical works in a jar. That is a blockage downstream of the pump. A lost prime usually gives low rather than high discharge pressure, and raw demand is unchanged.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms a recurring injection point blockage?

options.label: Archived alum supplier strength certificates
Archived raw water turbidity trend
Archived maintenance log for the injection quill and feed line

nextClue.explanation: Archived maintenance log for the injection quill and feed line directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Supplier certificates show the alum met specification, matching the good jar test result.
clueText.nc-b: Raw turbidity was flat all shift, which rules out a demand surge.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the quill was last cleaned 14 months ago and has plugged twice before with the same high pressure and zero tank drawdown.

tasks.prompt: Floc in the flocculation basin at a Saskatchewan plant is patchy, with dense clouds of good floc beside stretches of milky untreated looking water, and settled turbidity is poor.
